title: Require context-length portfolios before removing compilation or execution guards

source.title: Internal RTX 4060 recurrent-chunk compiler-disable fresh-process paired screen
source.claim_scope: Removing torch.compiler.disable from one recurrent chunk rule improved a smoke case, but the first frozen fresh-process portfolio repeat regressed weighted TTFT to 0.988924x; T128 improved while T512 and T2048 regressed. This is a single-task context guard, not a cross-framework policy verdict.

implementation_recipe: Treat removal of a compiler or execution guard as a context-sensitive candidate, not as a universally beneficial simplification.
Freeze a production-weighted context-length portfolio before measuring the candidate.
Run each arm in a fresh process when compilation state, graph state or cache reuse can otherwise leak across arms.
Retain a context guard or reject the candidate when short-context gains do not survive the weighted portfolio.
validation_recipe: Record per-context correctness, latency and backend realization for unchanged control and candidate.
Require every repeat to pass the frozen weighted gate; stop early when remaining repeats cannot mathematically recover the decision.
Report per-context direction so a short-sequence gain cannot hide medium- or long-context regressions.
Do not translate compile-state smoke results into whole-workload, production or cross-framework claims.
expected_bottleneck_shifts: Guard removal may reduce fixed launch or graph overhead at short contexts while exposing compilation, memory or kernel inefficiency at longer contexts.
Portfolio early-stop redirects GPU budget from an unrecoverable candidate to a different removable-work hypothesis.
failure_modes: A single short-context smoke result is treated as representative of the production context distribution.
Warm process state is reused across arms and attributed to the code change.
An aggregate median hides a required context bucket regression.
The guard is removed before backend realization and correctness are checked.
scope_limits: The RTX 4060 recurrent-chunk result does not prove that compiler guards should remain on other operators or hardware.
A failed weighted portfolio may still justify a narrowly declared short-context specialization after separate production-share analysis.
This revision changes candidate validation and claim scope only; it is not performance evidence for a new implementation.

candidate_archetypes.name: portfolio-qualified compiler guard removal
candidate_archetypes.template: Freeze short, medium and long context buckets, compare unchanged and guard-removed arms in fresh processes, and retain the change only in buckets whose correctness and paired performance gates pass.
